stories.title: Bose's noise-cancelling earbuds that never need charging
stories.dek: They plug into USB-C and take power from your phone or laptop, so there's no battery to run flat. They're sold out in most places.
stories.why: Noise cancelling without ever needing to charge is handy for flights and long days.
points: Plug into USB-C and draw power from your phone or laptop, so there's no battery.
Active noise cancelling with a three-button inline remote.
£99 / $99, in black, white or mint. Sold out in many places.

body.p: Bose's new noise-cancelling earbuds have no battery at all. They plug into a USB-C port and draw power from your phone or laptop.
Wireless earbuds need charging and wear out over time. These skip both problems, which makes them handy for flights and long days, and they're cheaper than most Bose earbuds.
They cost £99 or $99, come in black, white or mint, and have a three-button remote. They've sold out in many places, so stock may be patchy for a while.

stories.title: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro clash in Brazil's first run-off debate
stories.dek: The two candidates traded attacks ahead of the 25 October presidential run-off.
points: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro met in their first run-off debate.
The run-off vote is on 25 October.

body.p: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro traded insults and accusations of lying and corruption in their first run-off debate in São Paulo on 18 October.

Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, finished first in the 4 October first round with about 47%, ahead of Lula on about 45%. They clashed over crime, healthcare, the cost of living and government spending, and Flávio faced questions about his father's handling of COVID-19.
Polls show a tight race with Flávio slightly ahead. A second debate is on 23 October, and Brazil votes in the run-off on 25 October.

stories.title: Cyprus may avoid the worst of a record El Niño
stories.dek: Forecasters expect a very strong El Niño this winter, but Cyprus looks likely to escape its harshest effects.
points: Forecasters expect a very strong El Niño over winter 2026–27.
Cyprus looks likely to escape its worst effects.

body.p: Forecasters say Cyprus could get much more rain than usual this autumn as one of the strongest El Niño events on record builds.

El Niño is a warming of the Pacific Ocean that shifts weather around the world. This one could push sea temperatures about 3.7°C above normal, bringing floods, droughts and wildfires to different regions. Globally, 2027 is very likely to be the hottest year on record.

For Cyprus, rainfall from October to December is forecast to be 20–70% above normal depending on the area, with October the wettest relative to usual. From December to February, rain is expected to be near or slightly below normal.

stories.title: What Cyprus's new cost-of-living package actually saves you
stories.dek: The €70m package cuts heating oil tax, extends electricity subsidies and zeroes VAT on some essentials. Economists say it barely touches energy bills, with inflation at 5.2%.
stories.why: It shows what help you actually get with bills this winter, and how little it covers.
points: A €70 million package from the government.
Heating oil tax falls from 7.4 to 2.1 cents a litre from 1 November, worth about €32 over a winter.
Electricity subsidies extended, zero VAT on some essentials, and lower VAT on home solar.
Inflation in Cyprus was 5.2% in August, third highest in the EU.

body.p: The government's new €70 million package is meant to ease the cost of living this winter, but economists say it barely touches high energy bills.

The package cuts tax on heating oil from 7.4 to 2.1 cents a litre from 1 November, extends electricity subsidies, removes VAT from some essential goods, lowers VAT on home solar panels and adds help for vulnerable households. The heating-oil cut saves an average home about €32 over a winter. Inflation in Cyprus hit 5.2% in August, the third highest in the EU, and economists blame energy costs.

The president says total relief spending tops €1 billion, but Cyprus Mail's own count of the listed packages comes to €545 million. Expect more pressure for help with electricity bills as winter goes on.

stories.title: DeLorean is entering an electric flying-car racing series
stories.dek: DeLorean becomes the first American constructor in Airspeeder, where piloted electric aircraft race each other. The aircraft design and pilots haven't been revealed yet.
stories.why: Flying-car racing is being used to test tech that could one day power air taxis.
points: DeLorean is the first American constructor in Airspeeder.
Races use piloted electric aircraft with AI-assisted safety systems.
The 2026–27 season starts in November.
DeLorean hasn't shown its aircraft or named pilots yet.

body.p: DeLorean is joining Airspeeder, a racing series for piloted electric flying cars. It becomes the first American constructor in the championship, and its team will race from the season that starts in November.

DeLorean is best known for the stainless-steel DMC-12 from Back to the Future, and the revived brand has been looking for ways to build on that name. Airspeeder races small electric aircraft, called speeders, that fly low over a set course with AI-assisted safety systems. The organisers see the racing as a testbed for future air taxis.
DeLorean hasn't shown its aircraft or named its pilots, and the race calendar hasn't been confirmed. Expect those details closer to the season opener.

stories.title: Cyprus pushes to delay the EU carbon charge on fuel and heating
stories.dek: ETS2 would put a carbon price on road fuel and heating from 2028. Cyprus, Greece, Italy and others want it pushed back, and Christodoulides says the Commission is listening.
stories.why: If ETS2 goes ahead, petrol, diesel and heating in Cyprus are likely to cost more from 2028.
points: ETS2 puts a carbon price on fuel for cars and heating, starting in 2028.
Cyprus, Greece, Italy and the Visegrad countries want it delayed.
President Christodoulides says the Commission understands the need to postpone it.
One party leader claims existing carbon charges already make up a fifth of power bills.

body.p: Cyprus is pushing for a delay to ETS2, the EU's new carbon charge on fuel for cars and heating. President Christodoulides says the European Commission now understands the need to postpone it.

The EU agreed in 2023 to put a carbon price on road fuel and heating, on top of the existing system for power plants and industry. It's due to start in 2028, after already being pushed back a year. Part of the money is meant to go into a Social Climate Fund to help poorer households. Cyprus, Greece, Italy and several Central European countries argue that adding costs during an energy crisis is the wrong move.
Any delay needs agreement at EU level. Some countries want it pushed back to 2030. If it goes ahead in 2028, expect petrol, diesel and heating oil in Cyprus to cost more.

stories.title: France and Germany want to soften the EU's 2035 petrol and diesel ban
stories.dek: Their plan would require a 90% cut in carmakers' CO2 by 2035 instead of 100%, leaving room for some combustion cars. Other EU countries and Parliament still have to agree.
stories.why: It could decide whether you can still buy a new petrol or hybrid car in the EU after 2035.
points: The current plan effectively bans new petrol and diesel cars from 2035.
France and Germany want a 90% CO2 cut instead of 100%, leaving room for some combustion cars.
Cars already on the road would not be banned.
Other EU countries and the European Parliament still need to agree.

body.p: France and Germany have agreed a joint plan to soften the EU's planned 2035 ban on new petrol and diesel cars.

Under EU law passed in 2023, new cars sold from 2035 must produce zero CO2, which effectively ends new petrol, diesel and most hybrid sales. Carmakers have struggled with slow EV sales and Chinese competition. The Franco-German plan would require a 90% cut instead, leaving room for some combustion engines and alternative fuels, and ties the change to support for cars made in Europe.
It's only a joint position for now. Other EU countries and the European Parliament must agree. Cars already on the road wouldn't be affected either way.

stories.title: EU leaders want a joint plan to bring energy prices down
stories.dek: At last week's summit they asked Brussels for short-term help for households and businesses and floated buying energy together. Nobody expects a quick deal, and diesel is set to stay expensive into 2027.
stories.why: Cyprus has some of the EU's highest electricity prices, so any EU-wide help could lower your bills.
points: Leaders asked Brussels for short-term support for households and businesses.
Ideas include extra aid for the hardest-hit sectors and buying energy jointly.
Greece's PM said not to expect a quick deal.
The IEA expects diesel to stay expensive into 2027.

body.p: At their summit on 15–16 October, EU leaders asked the European Commission for a joint plan to tackle soaring energy prices.

Energy costs have jumped again, partly because of the war involving Iran, which has disrupted oil and gas markets. Cyprus is hit especially hard: it's not connected to Europe's gas or power grids and still makes most of its electricity from imported oil.

Ideas on the table include short-term help for households and businesses, extra aid for the hardest-hit industries and buying energy jointly. Greece's prime minister warned not to expect a quick deal, and the International Energy Agency expects diesel to stay expensive into 2027.

stories.title: Macron condemns rioting as protests spread across France
stories.dek: Student protests over school funding, joined by the Gilets Jaunes, turned violent on Saturday with about 2,400 arrests. No state of emergency has been declared.
stories.why: France is a major EU economy, and the unrest is driven by the same living-cost pressures felt across Europe.
points: It started with student blockades over school funding, then the Gilets Jaunes joined over costs and fuel prices.
Saturday saw some of the worst urban violence in years: about 2,400 arrests and around 1,000 police hurt.
Macron condemned the rioting but did not declare a state of emergency or curfew.

body.p: France saw some of its worst urban violence in years on Saturday, with looting and clashes across the country. About 2,400 people were arrested and around 1,000 police and gendarmes were injured.

The protests began with students blockading schools and universities over underfunding, crumbling buildings and teacher shortages. They grew when the Gilets Jaunes joined over the cost of living, austerity and fuel prices. The Gilets Jaunes movement first appeared in 2018 over a fuel tax rise.

President Macron condemned the violence in a TV address and said rioters would be punished, but he stopped short of a state of emergency or curfew. More protests are likely as long as the cost-of-living pressure continues.

stories.title: This week's menswear: a NOMOS worldtimer, Loro Piana and Crockett & Jones
stories.dek: The Gentleman's Journal's five standout releases this week, from a blue-dial watch to suede loafers.
stories.why: A quick way to see what's new and worth knowing in menswear without trawling through shops.
points: Five picks covering a watch, a winter coat, knitwear, a shirt and shoes.
Prices run from £155 for a lambswool jumper to £3,410 for the coat.

items.name: Zürich Worldtimer, Midnight Blue
items.note: A 40 mm watch that shows the time in every world time zone.

items.name: Kensington Coat
items.note: A winter overcoat in Pecora Nera wool.

items.name: Raspberry Lambswool Crew Neck
items.note: A bright lambswool jumper to lift a plain autumn outfit.

items.name: White Oxford Shirt
items.note: Cut and sewn by hand in white Oxford cotton.

items.name: Boston 2, Dark Oak Suede
items.note: A suede loafer from the Northampton shoemaker.

body.p: The Gentleman's Journal picked five new menswear releases this week, from a worldtimer watch to suede loafers.
This week leans into autumn: a heavyweight winter coat, a bright lambswool jumper, a crisp Oxford shirt and loafers in dark suede.
Prices range from £155 for the jumper to £3,410 for the Loro Piana coat. See the picks below.

stories.title: GTA 6's launch trailer is out, captured on a standard PS5
stories.dek: Rockstar's final trailer is mostly cinematic, with Jason and Lucia front and centre. Justice wrote the whole score, and the game is about a month away. PC is rumoured for early 2027.
stories.why: GTA 6 is the biggest game release in years, and it's now about a month away.
points: The launch trailer is mostly cinematic, featuring Jason and Lucia.
All footage was captured on a standard PS5; the game runs at 30 fps on console.
Electronic duo Justice wrote the full score.
Pre-orders are $79.99. A PC version is rumoured for early 2027.

body.p: Rockstar has released the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI, about a month before release. It's mostly cinematic, featuring the two lead characters, Jason and Lucia.

GTA VI is the first new main GTA game since GTA V in 2013, which became one of the best-selling games ever. The new game returns to Vice City in the state of Leonida, Rockstar's take on Florida. Its release has already slipped once, so this trailer is a strong sign it's on track.

All the footage was captured on a standard PS5, and the game runs at 30 fps on consoles. The French duo Justice wrote the full score. Pre-orders are $79.99, with a bonus pack if you order before 20 November. A PC version is rumoured for early 2027 but not confirmed.

stories.title: Harley's cheapest-ever bike, the Sprint, is nearly here
stories.dek: Harley-Davidson's new entry-level model is close to its global reveal.
stories.why: A cheaper Harley could bring the brand within reach of newer riders.
points: The Sprint will be Harley-Davidson's most affordable bike.
Its global reveal is close.

body.p: Harley-Davidson's new entry-level bike, the Sprint, is close to its global reveal. It's set to be the cheapest Harley yet.
Harley has been trying to reach younger and newer riders, who often find its big cruisers too expensive and heavy. A smaller, cheaper model could bring them into the brand.
Specs and pricing will come with the official reveal, expected soon.

stories.title: Royal Enfield's Himalayan 750 spotted almost ready
stories.dek: The bigger twin-cylinder Himalayan, on Royal Enfield's new 750 platform, has been seen in near-final form ahead of its EICMA reveal.
stories.why: The Himalayan is one of the best-value adventure bikes, and a twin-cylinder version would take on bigger, pricier rivals.
points: Built on Royal Enfield's new 750cc twin-cylinder platform.
Spotted in near-final form, so the design is close to done.
Its official reveal is expected at EICMA in Milan, 5–8 November.

body.p: Royal Enfield's bigger Himalayan has been spotted in near-final form. It uses the company's new 750cc twin-cylinder engine, and its official debut is expected at EICMA in Milan in early November.

The Himalayan launched in 2016 as a simple, tough single-cylinder adventure bike, and the current 450 version has been a big hit for its price. A 750 twin would move it into the class of bikes like the Yamaha Ténéré 700 and Triumph Tiger 660, adding more power for motorway riding and carrying luggage.
Expect full specs and pricing at the EICMA reveal, with sales likely to follow in 2027.

stories.title: Honda's Rebel 500 gets E-Clutch for 2027
stories.dek: The cruiser adds Honda's clutchless-shifting system and a round 3.5-inch colour screen.
stories.why: E-Clutch lets you ride without touching the clutch lever, which makes an easy beginner bike even easier.
points: The 2027 Rebel 500 adds Honda's E-Clutch system.
It also gets a round 3.5-inch colour screen.

body.p: Honda's Rebel 500 cruiser gets the company's E-Clutch system for 2027, along with a new round 3.5-inch colour screen.

E-Clutch, first launched in 2024 on the CB650R and CBR650R, lets you pull away, stop and change gear without touching the clutch lever, while still letting you use it if you want. On the Rebel, already one of the easiest bikes for beginners, it makes riding in traffic even simpler.
The updated Rebel 500 is part of Honda's 2027 range. Pricing and arrival dates will vary by country.

stories.title: Hublot remakes its very first watch in solid gold
stories.dek: The Classic Fusion Tributo grows to 38mm and swaps quartz for an in-house automatic movement, on Hublot's signature black rubber strap.
stories.why: It's a modern take on the watch that started Hublot's rubber-strap-and-gold style.
points: Case grows from 36 mm to 38 mm, in yellow or white gold.
Swaps the original's quartz for an in-house automatic movement with 60 hours of reserve.
Black rubber strap and a see-through sapphire caseback.

body.p: Hublot has remade its very first watch as the Classic Fusion Tributo, in solid yellow or white gold on a black rubber strap.

When Hublot launched in 1980, pairing a gold watch with a rubber strap was unheard of, and it became the brand's signature. The original ran on quartz. The new version is slightly bigger at 38 mm and switches to an in-house automatic movement.
The movement gives 60 hours of power reserve and is visible through a sapphire caseback. It costs £23,600 or about €30,200.

stories.title: Kenya confirms its eighth Ebola case
stories.dek: The new patient was likely exposed to the country's first case, as a regional outbreak widens.
points: Kenya has confirmed its eighth case.
The new patient was likely exposed to the country's first confirmed case.
The outbreak is spreading across the region.

body.p: Kenya has confirmed its eighth Ebola case: a 49-year-old man who was likely exposed to the country's first patient. He has been quarantined.

The outbreak began in May in the Democratic Republic of Congo, centred on Ituri province, and has become the deadliest in the country's history, with at least 9,400 cases and more than 4,500 deaths. It's caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment; the main Ebola vaccine works only against a different strain.

Kenya is on heightened alert. In Congo, North Kivu province has banned arrivals from Ituri for a week, limited passengers in vehicles and suspended large gatherings. Neighbouring Uganda had 20 cases earlier and was declared Ebola-free in August.

stories.title: Klättermusen's sci-fi-looking freeride kit
stories.dek: The Swedish brand's first collection made for freeride skiing and snowboarding uses recycled fabrics, roomier cuts and built-in RECCO reflectors.
stories.why: It shows how serious ski kit is getting greener without losing performance.
points: Klättermusen's first collection made for freeride skiing and snowboarding.
Outer fabrics and insulation are 100% recycled, with a fluorocarbon-free water-repellent finish.
Built-in RECCO reflectors help rescuers find you.
Roomier cuts to fit layers underneath.

body.p: Swedish outdoor brand Klättermusen has launched The Signal, its first collection made specifically for freeride skiing and snowboarding.
Freeriding means skiing off-piste, away from groomed runs, where kit has to handle deep snow and rough conditions. Klättermusen is known for technical gear with a strong focus on sustainability.

The shells and insulation are fully recycled, with a water-repellent finish free of fluorocarbons. Some pieces have built-in RECCO reflectors that help rescuers find you in an avalanche, and the cuts are roomier to fit layers underneath.

stories.title: Daniel Craig plays the Magician in Netflix's Narnia
stories.dek: The Magician's Nephew gets a cinema release before it streams, with Emma Mackey as the White Witch.
points: Daniel Craig plays the Magician; Emma Mackey is the White Witch.
A Netflix film that opens in cinemas first, in February 2027.
Streaming date not announced yet.

body.p: Daniel Craig will play the Magician in Netflix's new Narnia film, The Magician's Nephew, with Emma Mackey as the White Witch.
The Magician's Nephew is C.S. Lewis's prequel, showing how Narnia began. Greta Gerwig is directing, and it's Netflix's first move to turn the books into a major film series.
It opens in cinemas first, in February 2027, before streaming on Netflix later. The streaming date hasn't been announced.

stories.title: How to dress for autumn, according to New & Lingwood
stories.dek: The Jermyn Street outfitter on tailoring and knitwear for the colder months.
stories.why: A quick guide to dressing well as the weather turns.
points: The London outfitter shares its rules for autumn tailoring.
Covers knitwear and layering for colder months.

body.p: New & Lingwood shares its rules for dressing well in autumn, from tailoring to knitwear.
New & Lingwood has made shirts and clothing on London's Jermyn Street since 1865, and it's known for classic British style with a playful edge.
Expect advice on layering, heavier fabrics and knitwear as the weather cools.

stories.title: Norton's first single-cylinder roadster debuts at EICMA
stories.dek: The TVS-owned British brand will show a new 450cc roadster in Milan, the first bike on a new platform that sits below the Atlas and Manx. Sales are expected in the second half of 2027.
stories.why: A 450cc single is the most popular kind of new bike right now, and Norton has never sold one in modern times.
points: Debuts at EICMA in Milan in November.
Estimated 40–45 hp from a liquid-cooled single with a six-speed gearbox (not confirmed).
First bike on a new platform, below the Atlas twin and the V4 Manx.
Built by owner TVS in India; on sale in the second half of 2027.

body.p: Norton will reveal a new 450cc single-cylinder roadster at EICMA in Milan in November. It's the first bike on a new, smaller platform and will sit below the twin-cylinder Atlas and the V4 Manx.

Norton is one of Britain's oldest motorcycle names, and India's TVS Motor bought it in 2020. The 400–450cc single-cylinder class is one of the busiest in motorcycling right now, with bikes like the Royal Enfield Himalayan 450, KTM 390 and Triumph Speed 400. A smaller Norton lets the brand reach far more riders.

Reported estimates put output at around 40–45 hp from a liquid-cooled engine with a six-speed gearbox, but Norton hasn't confirmed this. It will be built at TVS's plant in India and should go on sale worldwide in the second half of 2027.

stories.title: Nothing's next launch might be smart glasses
stories.dek: Carl Pei's company looks set to step beyond phones and earbuds. Here's what's known so far.
stories.why: Nothing is known for bold designs, so its first glasses could be an interesting rival to Meta's.
points: Nothing's next product is expected to be something other than a phone or audio device.
Reports point to smart glasses.

body.p: Nothing's next product looks set to be something new: reports point to smart glasses rather than another phone or pair of earbuds.

Nothing is the London company started in 2020 by Carl Pei, a co-founder of OnePlus. It's known for see-through designs and glowing light patterns. Smart glasses are a fast-growing category, led by Meta's Ray-Ban glasses.
Nothing hasn't officially confirmed the product, so details on price, features and launch date are still to come.

stories.title: Pope Leo greeted by crowds after lung cancer surgery
stories.dek: It was his first major public appearance since the operation.
points: Pope Leo was greeted by crowds.
It was his first major appearance since lung cancer surgery.

body.p: Pope Leo addressed about 15,000 people in St Peter's Square on Sunday, his first major appearance since surgery for lung cancer.

He had a lung nodule removed on 13 October at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, and it was confirmed as adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. Leo XIV was elected in May 2025 and is the first pope born in the United States.

Tests to see whether the cancer has spread are still pending. He says he'll return to his duties gradually. A November trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru is in doubt, though his surgeon sees no medical reason to cancel it.

stories.title: Porsche's Mission S is a mid-engined supercar, and it isn't electric
stories.dek: Revealed in New York, the Mission S concept previews a car that would sit above the 911. Porsche hasn't shared engine or power figures yet, and the production version could look different.
stories.why: Porsche hasn't had a model above the 911 since the 918 Spyder, and this one keeps a combustion engine while rivals go electric.
points: Shown as a concept in New York, so the production car may look different.
Mid-engined and not electric. Porsche hasn't confirmed the engine or power.
It would sit above the 911 in Porsche's range.
No price or launch date yet; early guesses start around £200,000.

body.p: Porsche has shown the Mission S, a concept for a new mid-engined supercar that would sit above the 911 as the brand's flagship. It was unveiled in New York, and unlike most recent Porsche concepts it isn't electric.

Porsche's halo cars have always been rare: the Carrera GT in the mid-2000s and the hybrid 918 Spyder a decade later. Since then the 911 has been the top of the range, while the brand's big bets went into electric cars like the Taycan. Keeping a combustion engine here is a sign that Porsche thinks buyers at this level still want one.

Porsche hasn't said what engine it uses, how powerful it is, or when it might go on sale. Concepts often change before production, so treat the design as a preview. Early estimates put the price somewhere above £200,000.

stories.title: RedMagic 12 Pro: a liquid-cooled gaming phone with a giant battery
stories.dek: It runs Qualcomm's newest chip with RGB liquid cooling built in. Global launch is expected on 3 November, and the price should undercut most flagships.
stories.spec: 8,400 mAh · 120 W wired · from ~$1,040 in China
stories.why: It packs flagship gaming power and a huge battery for much less than most top phones.
points: Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chip.
8,400 mAh battery with 120 W wired and 80 W wireless charging.
Built-in RGB liquid cooling to keep it fast during long gaming sessions.
Starts at about $1,040 in China; global launch expected 3 November.

body.p: RedMagic, the gaming-phone brand from Nubia, has launched the 12 Pro in China. It combines Qualcomm's newest top chip with a huge battery and built-in liquid cooling, at a lower price than most flagships.

Gaming phones are built to keep performance high during long sessions, which ordinary phones struggle with when they heat up. RedMagic's party trick is active cooling, here an RGB-lit liquid system, plus fast charging.

Specs include an 8,400 mAh battery with 120 W wired and 80 W wireless charging. In China it starts at about $1,040. The global launch is expected on 3 November, when European prices should be announced.

stories.title: Rivian built a real Ghostbusters car on its R1S
stories.dek: The Ecto-R1 is a Halloween tie-in with Sony Pictures, complete with roof rack, lights and radar dish. Owners also get a themed over-the-air update with Ghostbusters lights and sounds until 2 November.
stories.why: A fun one: a real, drivable Ghostbusters car, and a themed update for Rivian owners.
points: Built on the Rivian R1S electric SUV, with the classic Ecto-1 look: white paint, red graphics, roof lights and a radar dish.
A Halloween tie-in with Sony Pictures.
Rivian owners get a Ghostbusters lights-and-sounds software update until 2 November.
The cars are for promotional events; there's no word on selling them.

body.p: Rivian has built a real-life Ghostbusters car on its R1S electric SUV. Called the Ecto-R1, it's a Halloween tie-in with Sony Pictures, finished in white with red graphics, a roof rack, emergency lights and a radar dish.
The original Ecto-1 from the 1984 film was a converted 1959 Cadillac ambulance, and it's one of the most famous movie cars ever. Rivian's version swaps the V8 for electric motors but keeps the look.

Rivian owners also get a themed software update with Ghostbusters lights, sounds and games, available until 2 November. The physical cars are for promotional events, and there's no sign they'll be sold.

stories.title: Trump defends easing sanctions on Russia
stories.dek: The US president justified the move and criticised Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
stories.why: Sanctions on Russia affect energy markets and the war in Ukraine, both of which shape prices in Europe.
points: Trump defended easing some US sanctions on Russia.
He also criticised Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

body.p: The Trump administration has waived or blocked a number of sanctions on Russia days before they were due to start, and has allowed Russia to sell more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel to world markets.

Trump says the aim is to keep Moscow involved in peace talks over Ukraine, and that the diesel will help bring down fuel prices, which rose after the US-Israeli war with Iran. European governments and many US officials have criticised the move as rewarding Russia while the war continues.
Zelenskyy says the waivers will strengthen Russia's war effort; Trump has accused him of not wanting to end the war. Talks between Ukraine and US envoys are continuing.

stories.title: The tiny two-seat Smart is back, now fully electric
stories.dek: The new Smart #2 is a proper city car again, with a Brabus version on the way. UK sales start next year.
stories.why: A small, cheap electric two-seater is exactly the kind of car that suits tight city streets and short trips.
points: Two doors, two seats, fully electric.
35.8 kWh battery for up to 205 miles of range.
60 kW (82 hp) motor; fast-charges from 10 to 80% in under 20 minutes.
Expected under £20,000 in the UK, with sales from next year. A Brabus version is planned.

body.p: Smart is bringing back a tiny two-seat city car, this time fully electric. It's called the #2, and a sportier Brabus version is also on the way. UK sales start next year at under £20,000.

Smart made its name with the Fortwo, the small two-seater that could park nose-first into a kerb. The brand, now owned jointly by Mercedes-Benz and Geely, has spent the last few years making bigger electric SUVs such as the #1 and #3. The #2 is a return to its roots.

The numbers suit city life: about 205 miles of range from a 35.8 kWh battery, an 82 hp motor, and fast charging from 10 to 80% in under 20 minutes. Details of the Brabus model, and of sales outside the UK, haven't been announced yet.

stories.title: Sony's new flagship Walkmans are back for serious listeners
stories.dek: Two new hi-res players, the top one with a gold-plated copper body and Kimber Kable wiring inside. Pre-orders are open now.
stories.why: These are some of the best dedicated music players you can buy, for people who want better sound than a phone.
points: Two models: the WM1AM3 and the top WM1ZM3.
The ZM3 has a gold-plated copper body with Kimber Kable wiring inside.
Hi-res and DSD playback, a 5.5-inch screen and up to 35 hours of battery.
From £2,099 / €2,499; shipping starts 27 November.

body.p: Sony has launched two new top-end Walkman music players, the WM1AM3 and the flagship WM1ZM3, for people who want better sound than a phone gives.

The Walkman name goes back to 1979. Today's high-end models are for listeners with large music libraries and good headphones. The ZM3 has a gold-plated copper body with Kimber Kable wiring inside, all aimed at cleaner sound.

Both play hi-res and DSD files, can stream over Wi-Fi, and last up to 35 hours. Prices start at £2,099 or €2,499 for the AM3, rising to £4,299 or €4,999 for the ZM3. Pre-orders are open, and shipping starts 27 November.

stories.title: Property of the week: a Grade I estate in Leicestershire
stories.dek: Stapleford Park, a historic country estate, is on the market.
points: A Grade I listed country estate in Leicestershire, England.
On the market for £18 million.

body.p: Stapleford Park, a Grade I listed country estate in Leicestershire, is on the market.
Grade I is the highest level of protection for historic buildings in England, given to only a small share of listed buildings.
The asking price is £18 million.

stories.title: Street Fighter wins the weekend box office
stories.dek: The video-game adaptation opened at No. 1 in the US, ahead of new horror You Can See Everything. Last week's winner, Other Mommy, dropped to third.
stories.why: A big win for video-game movies, which are now a reliable box-office draw.
points: Opened at No. 1 in the US with about $31 million.
Horror film You Can See Everything came second with about $15 million.
Whalefall and a new Sense and Sensibility also opened in the top five.
Last week's No. 1, Other Mommy, dropped to third.

body.p: The new Street Fighter film opened at No. 1 in the US with about $31 million, beating four other new releases.
Street Fighter started as a Capcom arcade game in 1987, and its first film in 1994 was a famous flop. Video-game films have since become a reliable box-office draw, so this result fits the trend.
Horror film You Can See Everything came second with about $15 million, while Whalefall and a new Sense and Sensibility also made the top five. Last week's winner, Other Mommy, fell to third.

stories.title: Suunto's titanium Race 3S goes longer on GPS
stories.dek: A lighter titanium sports watch that Suunto says lasts much longer with GPS running than the model it replaces.
stories.why: Longer GPS battery means fewer charges for runners and hikers.
points: A titanium sports watch from Suunto.
Suunto says GPS battery life is about 40% longer.

body.p: Suunto has launched the Race 3S, a titanium sports watch that it says lasts about 40% longer with GPS running than before.
Suunto is a Finnish brand with a long history in outdoor and dive instruments. GPS battery life is the number that matters most for runners, hikers and cyclists on long days out.
The Race 3S takes on Garmin's Forerunner and Fenix watches. Check Suunto's site for pricing and full specs.

stories.title: Triumph teases new Tiger 900, Tiger 1200 and Street Triple for 2027
stories.dek: Three big updates are coming, plus new A2-licence-friendly Bonneville models.
stories.why: The Tiger 900 and Street Triple are two of Triumph's best sellers, so new versions matter for anyone shopping mid-size bikes.
points: Triumph has teased new 2027 versions of the Tiger 900, Tiger 1200 and Street Triple.
New A2-licence-friendly Bonneville models are coming too.
Full details are expected at the launch.

body.p: Triumph has teased new 2027 versions of three key bikes: the Tiger 900 and Tiger 1200 adventure bikes and the Street Triple naked bike. It's also adding new Bonneville models aimed at riders on an A2 licence.

The Tiger 900 and Street Triple are among Triumph's best sellers, so updates to them matter for anyone shopping for a mid-size bike. A2-friendly models are designed for newer riders, who are limited to 35 kW until they move up to a full licence.
Triumph hasn't released full details yet. Launch dates and specs should follow soon, probably around the big autumn motorcycle shows.

stories.title: Four Central European states ask the EU to slow its Russian energy phase-out
stories.dek: Poland, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary want more time under the EU's plan to stop buying Russian energy.
stories.why: How fast the EU drops Russian energy affects gas and fuel prices across the bloc, Cyprus included.
points: Poland, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary want more time to phase out Russian energy.
They're asking Brussels to loosen the rules.

body.p: Poland, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary, the Visegrad Four, are asking Brussels for more flexibility on the EU's plan to stop buying Russian energy by 2027.

As landlocked countries that depend on old pipeline routes, they say switching suppliers is harder and costlier for them. Electricity futures in Central Europe are more than 60% above pre-crisis levels. They also want EU money for new oil and gas infrastructure and, like Cyprus, a delay to the ETS2 carbon charge until 2030.

The EU's energy commissioner acknowledged the problem but wants only targeted, temporary measures. Hungary is also challenging the phase-out in an EU court, with a first ruling expected in a few months.

stories.title: Eight firms bid to finish the stalled Vasiliko gas terminal
stories.dek: The terminal is meant to bring cheaper gas for electricity, but after €300m spent it still isn't running. Gas-fired power isn't expected before 2030.
stories.why: Without gas, Cyprus keeps making electricity from expensive oil, which is a big reason bills are high.
points: Eight companies want the job of finishing the terminal.
About €300 million has already been spent, and finishing it is estimated at €180 million.
Even with a contract by summer 2027, gas power isn't expected before 2030.

body.p: Eight companies have expressed interest in finishing the Vasiliko gas import terminal, a project that has already cost about €300 million without ever working.

The terminal is supposed to let Cyprus import liquefied natural gas to run its power stations. Today Cyprus burns oil to make electricity, which is expensive and polluting, and it's the only EU country not connected to Europe's gas or power networks. That's a big reason electricity bills here are so high.
Finishing the job is estimated at €180 million. Even if a contract is signed by summer 2027, gas-fired power isn't expected before 2030.

stories.title: Xbox Nano is a smaller controller built for cloud gaming
stories.dek: Microsoft's new compact pad is aimed at playing Xbox Cloud Gaming on phones, tablets and TVs without a console.
stories.why: Cloud gaming lets you play Xbox games without a console, and a smaller pad makes that easier on the go.
points: A new, more compact Xbox controller.
Designed for Xbox Cloud Gaming on phones, tablets and TVs.

body.p: Microsoft has announced the Xbox Nano, a smaller controller designed for Xbox Cloud Gaming.
Cloud gaming streams games from Microsoft's servers, so you can play Xbox titles on a phone, tablet or TV without a console. A compact controller makes that easier to carry around.
Microsoft hasn't shared full pricing or availability in this report. Expect it to be sold alongside Game Pass, which includes cloud gaming.
